source_documents.title: Formyl‐Group Multiplicity Regulates Nonradiative Decay Through Intermolecular Locking in Tetraphenylethylene‐Based Aggregation‐Induced Emission Luminogens

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, aggregation alone does not guarantee high solid-state photoluminescence efficiency, because residual molecular motions may still promote nonradiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-nCHO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Residual motions in some aggregates keep nonradiative decay active.

reference_evidence_units.quote: TPE-CHO shows only 20 ± 2%, whereas (Z)-TPE-2CHO, (E)-TPE-2CHO, and TPE-4CHO reach 89 ± 2%, 99 ± 1%, and 99 ± 1%, respectively.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-CHO, (E)-TPE-2CHO, TPE-4CHO

reference_evidence_units.quote: Fluorescence lifetime analysis shows that the low efficiency of TPE-CHO is associated with a substantially larger nonradiative decay contribution.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-CHO
reference_evidence_units.statement: knr is much larger for the mono-aldehyde.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Single-crystal structures and quantitative short-contact statistics indicate that the highly emissive (E)-TPE-2CHO and TPE-4CHO crystals possess more extensive and spatially distributed intermolecular contact networks than TPE-CHO.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-CHO, (E)-TPE-2CHO, TPE-4CHO
reference_evidence_units.statement: More short contacts around the bright crystals.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Importantly, these results reveal that aggregation activates fluorescence in all four compounds, but does not suppress nonradiative decay to the same extent.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four
reference_evidence_units.statement: All are AIE-active, with different residual knr.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These results support a twisting–locking design picture in which molecular twisting prevents unfavorable π–π stacking, while multipoint intermolecular contacts provide structural confinement that is consistent with reduced nonradiative relaxation.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-nCHO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Twisting prevents stacking; contacts lock the flexible TPE frame.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We emphasize, however, that the crystallographic observations provide structural support rather than direct dynamic evidence of restricted molecular motion, and that the quantitative photophysical parameters were measured for powders.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-nCHO
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors flag that restricted motion is inferred, not measured.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Its AIE behavior is generally attributed to the restriction of intramolecular motion: phenyl-ring rotation and excited-state structural relaxation efficiently dissipate energy in solution, whereas aggregation suppresses these motions and activates fluorescence [13–16].
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE scaffold
reference_evidence_units.statement: Phenyl rotation and relaxation quench in solution; aggregation restricts them.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: From earlier work, not re-measured here.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: AIE from restricted phenyl rotation/relaxation; intermolecular contact networks lock residual motion and set knr. The authors note this is structural support, not dynamic evidence (E07). PLQY 99%.

contrast_group.varied_factor: number of para-formyl groups on tetraphenylethylene (1 vs 2 trans vs 4)
contrast_group.paper_difference: All are AIE-active, but the mono-aldehyde keeps a large knr (PLQY 20%) while the di- and tetra-aldehydes, locked by denser intermolecular contacts, reach 99%.
